title: Vaults GG MUSIC TEST (VRUN: Vaults of Obsolete Code on the Game Gear: its music as a player ROM)
description: The music test spinoff of the Game Gear port (project vrun-voc-gg), modelled on CTW NES's AudioPlayer: the game's real sound unit (src/voc_sound.c, the same file the game builds: the PSG music driver), the song list (all 22 tracks of the game) and one FL TEST slot (list 23), nothing else. musictest/build_musictest.ps1 makes the songs the game's way (the Game Boy version's roster through its musictest/make_roster.py + tools/music/convert.py, then tools/psg/convert_music.py with --extra-track for the FL TEST slot) and builds build.ps1 -Target musictest (the game target is unchanged). Mute / solo without touching the driver: a muted channel is marked as an effect's (sfx_busy). An .flp song goes into the FL TEST slot with BrokenDev/tools/music/flp/musictest/build-vaults-gg-mt.ps1 (FruityHost mt-export vocgg).

toolchain: SDCC 4.6.0 and devkitSMS 533ae57, pinned in toolchains.json
Python 3 and the Game Boy version's tree (PROJECTS/VRUN_VOC_dev: its roster and converter)

steps.name: build
steps.note: musictest/build_musictest.ps1: the songs into build/musictest/gen, then build.ps1 -Target musictest -Extra <gen> (the toolchains at build.ps1's pinned defaults).

run.note: The first track plays at power-on. Up / Down a track, 1 play from the start, 2 stop, Left / Right a channel (T0 T1 T2 NS), Start+1 mute / unmute it, Start solo it (again: no solo). Songs loop. List 23 = FL TEST.

memory.what: the game's sound unit took the title track

scenarios.why: power-on: the list on screen, the first track sounds

memory.what: all four channels muted from the pad

scenarios.why: mute from the pad changes the output: the four channels muted = silence
the FL TEST slot plays (the placeholder here; an .flp's song with build-vaults-gg-mt.ps1)

knownIssues: The 22 tracks are the game's: today 11 placeholder songs; the GG driver plays the Game Boy song bytes (no duty / envelopes / pan, as in the game).
The user's songs are written with NES-console BrokenNes2 instances: mt-export reads them as Game Boy instances when a song has none for the Game Gear (a fence note says so).
